h1: Low-FODMAP Macro Calculator for IBS & SIBO
description: Calculate your low-FODMAP macros in seconds: 20% protein, 30% fat, 50% tolerated carbs (Monash protocol). Includes a food list and comparison table. Backed by 70% IBS symptom improvement evidence.
answerSnippet: On the low-FODMAP diet the standard macro split is **20% protein / 30% fat / 50% carbohydrates**, but carbs must come from low-FODMAP sources only (rice, potato, oats, ripe banana). For 2,000 kcal/day: 100 g protein + 67 g fat + 250 g tolerated carbs.
intro: The **low-FODMAP diet** (Monash University, 2005) removes short-chain carbohydrates that ferment in the intestine: **F**ermentable **O**ligosaccharides, **D**isaccharides, **M**onosaccharides **A**nd **P**olyols. It's the most evidence-backed dietary intervention for **irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)** and **SIBO**, improving symptoms in **70% of patients**. The standard macro distribution is **20% protein / 30% fat / 50% carbohydrates**, with carbs sourced exclusively from low-FODMAP foods. The protocol has 3 phases: **1) Elimination (2–6 weeks)**; **2) Gradual reintroduction (6–8 weeks)**; **3) Personalisation**.
keyTakeaway: Low-FODMAP macro split: **20% protein + 30% fat + 50% tolerated carbs**. For 2,000 kcal: 100 g protein + 67 g fat + 250 g carbs. 3 phases. 70% IBS symptom improvement.
useCases: Your gastroenterologist or dietitian recommended it.

example.title: Worked example: 2,000 kcal/day low-FODMAP plan
steps: **Fat (30%)**: `2000 × 0.30 / 9` = **67 g/day** — olive oil, avocado, aged cheese.
**Low-FODMAP carbs (50%)**: `2000 × 0.50 / 4` = **250 g/day** — rice, potato, carrot, quinoa, ripe banana.
example.result: Typical day: chicken breast + rice + carrot + strawberries + olive oil. Avoid onion, garlic, wheat, and lactose-containing dairy.

explanation:
## What is the Low-FODMAP Diet?

Developed at **Monash University (Australia)**, low-FODMAP temporarily removes short-chain carbohydrates that gut bacteria rapidly ferment, producing gas, bloating, and pain.

## The 5 FODMAP Groups to Restrict

| Group | High-FODMAP Foods |
|-------|-------------------|
| **Fructans** | Wheat, onion, garlic, leek |
| **GOS** | Legumes, broccoli, beetroot |
| **Lactose** | Milk, yogurt, ricotta |
| **Excess fructose** | Apple, mango, honey, pear |
| **Polyols** | Cherries, sorbitol, xylitol |

## Allowed Low-FODMAP Foods

| Category | Options |
|---------|---------|
| **Grains** | Rice, potato, quinoa, oats (½ cup cooked), polenta |
| **Protein** | Chicken, beef, fish, eggs, firm tofu |
| **Vegetables** | Tomato, cucumber, carrot, spinach, squash |
| **Fruit** | Strawberry, ripe banana, kiwi, orange, grapes |
| **Dairy** | Lactose-free options, aged cheese (cheddar, parmesan) |
| **Fats** | Olive oil, small portion of avocado |

## Macro Table by Calorie Level

| Calories | Protein | Fat | Carbs |
|----------|---------|-----|-------|
| 1,500 kcal | 75 g | 50 g | 188 g |
| 1,800 kcal | 90 g | 60 g | 225 g |
| 2,000 kcal | 100 g | 67 g | 250 g |
| 2,200 kcal | 110 g | 73 g | 275 g |
| 2,500 kcal | 125 g | 83 g | 313 g |

## The 3 Phases of the Monash Protocol

### Phase 1 – Elimination (2–6 weeks)
Remove all high-FODMAP foods completely. Most patients see significant symptom relief within 1–2 weeks.

### Phase 2 – Reintroduction (6–8 weeks)
Test one FODMAP group at a time: 3 test days (increasing portions) followed by 3 washout days. Identifies which specific groups trigger your symptoms.

### Phase 3 – Personalisation
Avoid only the groups that caused symptoms. Many people can reintroduce most foods after completing the protocol.

## Scientific Evidence

- **70% symptom improvement in IBS** (Gastroenterology meta-analysis, 2017, n=1,860).
- Strongest dietary evidence for IBS management.
- For SIBO, most effective in combination with antibiotic or herbal antimicrobial treatment.

## Related Tools

- [Histamine Intolerance Calculator](/calculadora-histamina-alimento-intolerancia).
- [Fructose Malabsorption](/calculadora-fructosa-malabsorcion).
- [Lactose Intolerance](/calculadora-lactosa-alimento-intolerancia).

**Not a permanent diet.** Long-term FODMAP elimination can negatively affect gut microbiota diversity. Always work with a registered dietitian.

faq.q: What is the standard low-FODMAP macro split?
faq.a: The Monash University protocol uses **20% protein, 30% fat, and 50% carbohydrates** as the starting distribution. The key constraint is that carbs must come from low-FODMAP sources — not from wheat, onion, garlic, legumes, or high-fructose foods.

faq.q: How many grams of carbs on low-FODMAP for 2,000 kcal?
faq.a: At 2,000 kcal with 50% carbs: `2000 × 0.50 / 4` = **250 g of carbohydrates per day**, from tolerated sources like rice, potato, quinoa, oats (½ cup cooked), ripe banana, strawberries, and carrots.

faq.q: How long does the elimination phase last?
faq.a: **2 to 6 weeks**, depending on symptom severity. It's not recommended to extend beyond 6–8 weeks because prolonged elimination can reduce gut microbiota diversity.

faq.q: Does the low-FODMAP diet cure IBS or SIBO?
faq.a: It doesn't cure either condition, but improves symptoms in **70% of IBS patients** (2017 meta-analysis). For SIBO, it works best when combined with antibiotic or herbal antimicrobial treatment prescribed by your doctor.

faq.q: Can vegetarians or vegans follow low-FODMAP?
faq.a: It's challenging but possible. Most plant proteins (legumes, seitan) are high-FODMAP. Tolerated options: **firm tofu** (not silken), **tempeh** (small portions), canned and rinsed chickpeas or lentils (max ¼ cup). A dietitian familiar with low-FODMAP is essential.

faq.q: What is Phase 2 and why does it matter?
faq.a: Phase 2 is the **reintroduction phase** (6–8 weeks). You test one FODMAP group at a time: 3 test days with increasing portions, then 3 washout days before testing the next group. This identifies *which* specific groups trigger your symptoms — most people are sensitive to only 1–2 groups, not all.

faq.q: What's the best app for checking FODMAP foods?
faq.a: The **Monash FODMAP app** (official, iOS and Android) is the gold standard — 1,000+ foods with red/yellow/green ratings by serving size. Also useful: FODMAP Friendly app.

faq.q: Is low-FODMAP a permanent eating plan?
faq.a: No. Elimination is temporary (2–6 weeks). After completing Phase 2 reintroduction, Phase 3 personalises your diet — most people avoid only the 1–3 groups that trigger their specific symptoms and eat freely otherwise.
